parsed.explanation: Civilian trans presentation is lawful, courts have remedied police bathroom advice, rejected mandatory surgery for recognition, and granted posthumous military reinstatement, showing recourse works. Persistent discrimination, no comprehensive anti-discrimination law, a hospitalisation blind spot with ministry refusal to draft guidelines, and organised violent opposition to Pride—with alleged police inaction at one event—create tier-3 hostility and care uncertainty. No civilian facility ban, birth-sex custody rule, border friction or organised visitor targeting is documented. Military-only same-sex criminalisation and resident LGR/school/work material do not directly expose a civilian visitor.

entry_documents.protection: Civilian same-sex conduct is lawful; no border trans-specific restriction is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport governs; military criminal code does not apply to a civilian visitor on stated facts.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Military-only consensual same-sex offence carries up to two years; 2017 saw 32 charges and one six-month sentence. Civilian trans-prisoner placement is undocumented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No civilian birth-sex placement rule is documented; district court remedied a military discharge posthumously.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Military exposure is documented, but it is not a civilian visitor detention regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Police advised a trans person to avoid public restrooms; trans teens avoid school restrooms for fear of outing, a resident indicator.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Final July 2024 judgment held police bathroom advice unlawful and awarded symbolic compensation against the state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No universal bathroom ban is documented; court protection counters the documented police advice.

care_services.exposure: National human rights commission flagged a transgender hospitalisation blind spot; health ministry refused to draft hospitalisation guidelines.
care_services.interaction: Emergency ward placement for a visitor is therefore uncertain, not a documented birth-sex rule.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised conservative and religious opposition, including violent Pride counter-protests; military trans exclusion and 2017 military witch hunt.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Free media and civil society; LGBTI registration ultimately won in court; courts have narrowed discriminatory requirements.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostility is societal and military-specific, while civilian courts have intervened for trans claimants.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans teens report avoiding school restrooms and pervasive discrimination; no traveller-family targeting is documented.
minors_guardians.protection: 2022 supreme court allowed legal recognition for unmarried trans parents with minor children; May 2024 court rejected mandatory surgery.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident family and school findings are climate signals; an adult travelling with a minor has no documented added border, care or custody exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: About 1,000 religious protesters attacked Pride participants in one city; organisers accused police of failing to act.
street_violence_police_response.protection: In another city 2,000 police protected 15,000 Pride attendees from violent counter-protesters in 2018.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response is uneven by event; capital LGBTQ neighbourhoods are described as broadly positive for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive anti-discrimination law; persistent documented discrimination; May 2020 contact tracing exposed LGBTQ identities and increased doxing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts awarded compensation for police rights infringement, rejected surgery mandates, and ordered posthumous reinstatement and line-of-duty recognition.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Individual litigation remedies operate, but systemic service and hospital protections are incomplete; several unknowns remain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: lawful expression, working courts and police protection in some cases, offset by persistent discrimination and uneven remedies. This case has stronger court remedies for bathroom and recognition claims, but a documented hospitalisation blind spot and violent Pride opposition keep it near this level.

Higher safety: acceptance is expressed through court compensation, lawful civilian status and positive capital neighbourhoods, but there is no documented traditional inclusion, routine service enforcement, or identity-based ward practice. Hospital and discrimination gaps make it lower than this anchor.

Much higher safety: there is no current survey showing a large majority of trans respondents refused or harassed in visitor-facing hotels, transport and shops, no unremedied universal exclusion, and courts have successfully remedied state conduct.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines lawful civilian status and demonstrably functioning courts with incomplete systemic protection. Police bathroom advice was remedied, creating a real limit on facility exposure, while the absence of a documented bathroom ban or civilian custody rule prevents a tier-1 rating. The main visitor-facing risks are social hostility and organised opposition, uneven police protection at public events, privacy outing, and uncertain emergency hospitalisation. Military criminalisation, trans military exclusion, LGR conditions and school/work discrimination mainly affect residents and do not establish a civilian visitor exposure. For a travelling adult with a minor, no additional documented rule is shown.
